precepts.text: He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken. The prophecy written of Christ.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Here is the prophecy about Christ: “He keepeth all his bones: not one of them is broken.”

What was commanded for the passover lamb in Exodus 12:46, “neither shall ye break a bone thereof”, is written here as a prophecy of the Messiah. Not one of his bones would be broken.

The passover is a representation of Christ laying down his life for us, and the Psalms spoke it ahead of time, so that when it came to pass we would know he is our passover.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them: the good angels deliver us from evil, like it says in the Lord's prayer.
precepts.point: What is Satan's job? To tempt us, and he is only allowed to do what God allows. God gave him the authority over all that Job had, but said, upon himself put not forth thine hand.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The angels minister unto the Most High, and they minister unto us. “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” These are the good angels. They encamp around them that fear him and deliver them from all evil, like it says in the Lord’s prayer.

Our forefathers never looked at the angels as some demonic thing that came down to earth to persecute and kill them. When three men stood by Abraham in the plains of Mamre, he ran to meet them, bowed himself, had water fetched to wash their feet and prepared a calf for them to eat. When two angels came to Sodom, Lot rose up to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground and made them a feast, and they did eat. They look like us.

The angel in Revelation told John, I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren; the angels have tribes too. Raphael presented the prayers of the saints. They are our brothers, working on our behalf. Calling them demons and fallen angels is Esau’s popular persuasion. The angel of the Lord camps round about them that fear God, just as the Lord set a hedge about Job, and delivers them.

precepts.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit and a broken and contrite heart, not so much an animal.
precepts.point: The Lord is nigh to them of a broken heart and saves such as be of a contrite spirit. Man by nature is arrogant, so the Lord has a way of breaking you down and shaming you until you say, I cannot do these things any more; I have to do better for the Lord's sake, for my own and for my people's as an example.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
David says it plainly: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” A sacrifice for the Lord is not so much an animal. What he wants laid on the altar is a broken spirit, a broken and contrite heart, which is a broken mind.

That is the same thing Psalms 34:18 says: “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart.” Man by nature is arrogant; we do what we want to do. So the Most High will put you in a position where he has to break you, break you down and shame you, bring you down to the lowest, until you realize: I can't do these things no more, I have to humble myself and do better, for the Lord's sake first and foremost, for my own sake, and for my people's sake as an example.

Isaiah shows where the Lord dwells when he comes near. “the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity” is the Father, and eternity is his domain, the upper room, the top floor. Yet he says, “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.” The Father and his Son deal with and dwell with the humble in spirit.

That broken spirit is the sacrifice worthy of his time. Being haughty and arrogant and offering the best sacrifices is a complete waste of time, because humility comes before honor. That is how Manasseh, a man the law said should die, found mercy: he humbled himself, and God would not despise that broken heart.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: The terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob. What Jacob feared after Shechem never came, because the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear Him and delivers them.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

That is why “the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.” After Shechem, Jacob feared the nations gathering against his house, but what he feared never came. The angel of the Lord encamped round about them and delivered them.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear Him, and delivereth them; Israelites that fear the Most High are guarded by His angels.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

The cloud and the fire upon the tabernacle were His angels, His created spirits, encamped round about the house of Israel throughout all their journeys. Israelites that fear the Most High are guarded by His angels and delivered.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, as David told us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 20: Laws of Warfare and the Spirit of Fear

precepts.why:
The priest told Israel at the battle: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, neither be ye terrified, “For the Lord your God is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.”

A lot of times you do not see that the Lord is fighting for you in the spirit; that is where faith comes in, for the Bible is a faith-based book. David told us how he fights for us: “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

You have to have faith that the Most High is fighting for you, with angels encamped round about the righteous, even when you cannot see them. That is the one that goeth with you to save you.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
precepts.point: Elisha prays that the Lord open the young man's eyes, and the Lord opens them so he sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. When Israel goes out to war, there is more with them than with their enemies, for the angels of the Lord are with them.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” That is what the young man saw when his eyes were opened.

The king of Syria sent “horses, and chariots, and a great host” by night to Dothan to fetch Elisha, and they compassed the city about. The servant rose early, saw the host, and cried, “Alas, my master! how shall we do?” Elisha answered, “Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” He prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and “behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.”

Round about the man of God, just as the psalm says the angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him. When Israel goes out to war, there is more with them than with their enemies, for the angels of the Lord are with them.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him and delivers them; this is the protection David prays for.
precepts.point: He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return, bring judgment on our enemies, and compass us round about with his angels.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
David prays for the Most High to arise and awake to the judgment he has commanded. Part of that prayer is protection: “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

That is the protection David asks for. He prays for the sake of the Israelites that the Lord will return, bring judgment on our enemies, and compass us round about with his angels. Those who fear the Most High are encamped about and delivered, while judgment falls on the enemies raging against them.

precepts.text: He also exalteth the horn of His people, the praise of all His saints, even of the children of Israel, showing His saints and His people are the same, the children of Israel near unto Him.
precepts.point: O fear the Lord ye His saints, for there is no want to them that fear Him. The young lions do lack and suffer hunger, but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing.

note.label: Psalm 34: I Will Bless the Lord at All Times

precepts.why:
“O fear the Lord, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.” Who are his saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” His saints and his people are the same: the children of Israel, a people near unto him.

So the saints told to taste and see that the Lord is good are the Israelites. Taste the commandments, taste these scriptures we should be reading day in and day out; this Bible is our daily bread. “blessed is the man that trusteth in him”: the man that trusts the words of this Bible and understands that it is a true book, our heritage, written to the Israelites in these last days. “The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing.”

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding, and in all thy ways acknowledge Him, which means keeping the commandments and being sincere in your prayers at all times, and He shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: The Lord redeemeth the soul of His servants, them that are out there doing the work putting the brick in that understanding mission, and none of them that trust in Him shall be desolate. None of us that trust in the Lord shall be destroyed, we are going to be redeemed from this captivity.

note.label: Psalm 34: I Will Bless the Lord at All Times

precepts.why:
“The Lord redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.” How do we trust him? “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.” Read on: in all thy ways acknowledge him, which means keeping the commandments and being sincere in your prayers at all times, and he shall direct thy paths.

That is us in this captivity: the brokenhearted, them of a contrite spirit, the last hired and the first fired, the ones they want to use as test dummies for a vaccine they created in under six months. “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart”, and we are the ones that need to be giving the Most High these praises; we are his people.

“Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but the Lord delivereth him out of them all.” “Evil shall slay the wicked: and they that hate the righteous shall be desolate”, so to the haters out there, you are going to be destroyed. But his servants, them that are out there doing the work, putting the brick in that understanding mission, trusting him with all their heart: none of them shall be destroyed. We are going to be redeemed from this captivity.

We are going to be afflicted; we got to be prepared for what is to come, prepared to be thrown in prison, to have our lives put on the line. How are we going to jeopardize our lives when we can't even get over depression, when we still turn to alcohol to get through the day? You are not ready to go across the world if you can't get over alcoholism in America.

note.label: The Bottle, the Battle, and the Bible

points: The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit. How is he near you? Through this Bible; you have the words to break it all. They did not count on us picking up this book and learning the truth of who we are, learning how to change our diet, control our desires, stop lying, and set up order and structure in our communities. And the Lord sent the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, to comfort us in our trauma. But you have to believe that you can heal from it.

TED talk played (about six minutes), from a pediatrician on childhood trauma: in the mid 90s the CDC and Kaiser Permanente discovered an exposure that dramatically increased the risk for seven out of ten of the leading causes of death in the United States; in high doses it affects brain development, the immune system, hormonal systems, and even the way DNA is read and transcribed, with triple the lifetime risk of heart disease and lung cancer and a twenty year difference in life expectancy. The exposure is childhood trauma: abuse, neglect, or growing up with a parent struggling with mental illness or substance dependence.

She opened a clinic in one of the poorest neighborhoods of San Francisco, and kids kept being referred for ADHD; but on a thorough history, most had experienced such severe trauma that something else was going on. In public health school they teach: if a hundred kids all drink from the same well and 98 of them develop diarrhea, you can write prescription after prescription, or you can walk over and ask what is in this well. The Lord is working on our people: writing the prescription keeps them rich, but she wanted to know why the people are sick.

The Adverse Childhood Experiences study asked seventeen and a half thousand adults about exposure to ACEs: physical, emotional, or sexual abuse; physical or emotional neglect; parental mental illness, substance dependence, incarceration; parental separation or divorce; domestic violence. Pause: did she not just describe our existence, everything our community has endured? ACEs are incredibly common: 67 percent of the population had at least one, and one in eight had four or more, with a dose response relationship: the higher the ACE score, the worse the health outcomes.

Back to Ecclesiasticus 40:8: such things happen unto all flesh, and that is sevenfold more upon sinners. And who did they teach to sin? What community do they keep in sin, knowing it leads to sickness later in life? The liquor store in our community, the drugs in our community, no banks, no loans; it is systematic, and every industry profits from what we have been through. This is why you brothers are called to heal: millions of our people are waiting on us to stand up, teach them the word of God, and help them heal.

From the ACE study PDF: the ACE score adds up the categories reported, from 0 to 10. The pyramid starts at adverse childhood experiences at the base, which lead to social, emotional, and cognitive impairment, which lead to the adoption of health risk behaviors, which lead to disease, disability, and social problems, and early death. Risk factors associated with the score: alcoholism, smoking, illicit drug use, obesity, suicide attempts, depression, anxiety, hallucinations, teen pregnancy, spontaneous abortion or fetal death, intimate partner violence, poor quality of life; diseases and early mortality: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, ischemic heart disease, liver disease, sexually transmitted diseases, lung cancer, death before age 65.

Definition read: a spontaneous abortion, more commonly known as a miscarriage, is the unexpected ending of a pregnancy before the 20th week, affecting roughly 10 to 20 percent of recognized pregnancies. Many of the miscarriages our sisters suffer stem from stress and trauma; the body cannot carry a certain stress level in pregnancy. You have to believe the word of God, forgive, and let go; it is affecting your body.

Neglect goes hand in hand with abuse: if a child was harmed, that child was also unprotected. And physical neglect is broader than we think: feeding children nothing but processed food and sugar, never teaching them to exercise or eat, tuning your children out and handing them a tablet instead of time; that is leading them down a path to be sick as adults. A child is supposed to be able to talk to their parents.
